text: Figure 3(b) presents the evolution of the peak cladding temperature as a function of time for the considered LOCA transient. Given the postulated scenario, the cold leg broke at 0.01 s and the scram initiated due to a low pressure signal at ~ 3.5 s. The power, then, started to decay, which led to the decrease of fuel temperature. Shortly afterward, the stored energy along with the decay energy heated up the fuel to the maximum value during the blowdown phase. Both the fuel and the cladding temperatures inflected once the core was reflooded, and finally got to the rewetting point. Zircaloy and duplex SiC cladding exhibit a similar history of fuel-centerline temperature. High thermal conductivity of tin gap and high heat capacity of SiC for the duplex concept yielded a slightly lower peak cladding temperature, despite of the low thermal conductivity of SiC which degraded the heat transfer from the fuel. The duplex design shows the lower blowdown and reflood temperature, which indicates good performance in heat removal during transient. Note that the integrity of the fuel was kept with a sufficient safety margin during LOCA for all concepts. The comparison of peak cladding temperature at the outer surface yields the same conclusion between fuel concepts. The duplex design shows the lower peak temperature and the shorter reflood phase. Overall, the duplex design exhibits a superior thermal-hydraulic performance during normal operation and the LOCA scenario.
